# Quick Overview

@stanleyOrderOperationsSociophonetic2022 proposes an order of operations for sociophonetic analysis as follows:

1.  Identify allophone categories.
2.  Identify outliers by allophone category.
3.  Carry out speaker normalization.

It's beyond the scope of `{tidynorm}` to define a pipeline for identifying allophone categories, since these will be extremely language, dialect, and label-set specific.
I would recommend reviewing the general purpose [`dplyr::case_when()`](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/case-and-replace-when.html) and [`dplyr::recode_values()`](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/recode-and-replace-values.html), or [`joeyr::code_allophones()`](https://joeystanley.github.io/joeyr/reference/code_allophones.html) for this step.

The second and third steps can be achieved in `{tidynorm}` by

2.  using `identify_outliers()`, `identify_track_outliers()` or `identify_dct_outliers()` to add an `.outlier` column to your vowel data frame.
3.  passing the `.outlier` column to `.exclude` in your normalization function.

Here is how `identify_outliers()` can be incorporated into a workflow normalizing point measures.

```{r}
speaker_data |>
  identify_outliers(
    # Use F1 through F3 to identify outliers
    F1:F3,

    # Identify outliers within speaker and
    # within vowel class
    .by = c(speaker, plt_vclass),

    # The probability level beyond which
    # rows are marked as outliers
    .level = 0.95
  ) |>
  norm_nearey(
    F1:F3,
    .by = speaker,

    # exclude rows marked as outliers
    .exclude = .outlier,
  ) ->
normed
```

- Both `identify_track_outliers()` and `identify_dct_outliers()` require a `.token_id_col` argument.

- `identify_dct_outliers()` requires a `.param_col` argument.

It's worth noting that passing an expression to `.exclude` only excludes data from the calculation of the normalization parameters.
All data points get normalized, so to remove outliers from the rest of your analysis flow, you'll need to do some additional filtering.

```{r}
nrow(speaker_data)
nrow(normed)
```

# Details

## General Info

The family of outlier identification functions add three new columns the input data frames:

`.mahal`

: The squared Mahalanobis distance.

`.prob`

: The probability of observing a value of `.mahal` this extreme or less.
  Based on the cumulative chi-squared probability distribution.

`.outlier`

: A logical vector indicating whether the vowel token exceeded the probability `.level` specified.

The Mahalanobis distance can be thought of as a multi-dimensional z-score.
For example, the two speakers in `speaker_data` have very different distributions for their \[æ\] vowel, and the outlier status for each token is specific to the shape of the distribution for each speaker for each vowel.

```{r}
speaker_data |>
  identify_outliers(
    F1:F2,
    .by = c(speaker, plt_vclass)
  ) |>
  filter(
    plt_vclass == "ae"
  ) ->
ae_identified
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: Plotting Code
ae_identified |>
  ggplot(
    aes(F2, F1)
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = sqrt(.mahal)),
    shape = 21
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    trans = c("log10", "reverse")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    trans = c("log10", "reverse")
  ) +
  expand_limits(
    fill = 0
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~speaker)
```

The `.prob` column is based on the chi-squared cumulative probability density function with degrees of freedom equal to the number of data dimensions.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: Plotting Code
ae_identified |>
  ggplot(
    aes(F2, F1)
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = .prob),
    shape = 21
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    trans = c("log10", "reverse")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    trans = c("log10", "reverse")
  ) +
  scale_fill_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~speaker)
```

## DCT and Track Outlier Identification

If you have a data frame of DCT coefficients by formant, `identify_dct_outliers()` will treat each DCT parameter for each formant as a data dimension over which the Mahalanobis distance is calculated.
For `identify_track_outliers()` each formant track first has the DCT transform applied, and then the Mahalanobis distance is calculated in the same way as `identify_dct_outliers()`.

```{r}
speaker_tracks |>
  identify_track_outliers(
    F1:F2,
    .by = c(speaker, plt_vclass),
    .token_id_col = id,
    .time_col = t,
    # DCT order
    .order = 5,
    .pre_trans = log,
    .return_dct = TRUE
  ) |>
  filter(plt_vclass == "ey") ->
ey_identified
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: Plotting Code
ey_identified |>
  reframe_with_idct(
    F1:F2,
    .by = c(speaker, id),
    .param_col = .param
  ) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(F2, F1)
  ) +
  geom_path(
    aes(
      color = .prob,
      group = id
    ),
    arrow = arrow(
      type = "closed",
      length = unit(0.1, "cm")
    )
  ) +
  scale_color_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  facet_wrap(~speaker)
```

# Extended uses

It's possible to use either the `.mahal` or `.prob` columns to calculate weighted means.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: Plotting Code
#| fig-asp: 0.5
ey_identified |>
  mutate(
    .inv_prob = 1 - .prob
  ) |>
  summarise(
    .by = c(speaker, .param),
    across(
      F1:F2,
      list(
        weighted = \(x) weighted.mean(x, .inv_prob),
        unweighted = mean
      )
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    starts_with("F")
  ) |>
  separate(
    name,
    into = c("formant", "weight")
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = formant,
    values_from = value
  ) |>
  reframe_with_idct(
    F1:F2,
    .by = c(speaker, weight),
    .param_col = .param
  ) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(F2, F1, color = weight)
  ) +
  geom_path(
    arrow = arrow(
      type = "closed",
      length = unit(0.1, "cm")
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  facet_wrap(~speaker)
```

It's also possible to use `1 - .prob` to carry out a weighted version of a standard normalization technique, down weighting outliers' contributions instead of categorically excluding them.

```{r}
speaker_data |>
  identify_outliers(
    F1:F3,
    .by = c(speaker, plt_vclass)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    .inv_prob = 1 - .prob
  ) |>
  # a weighted log-mean normalization
  norm_generic(
    F1:F3,
    .by = speaker,
    .pre_trans = log,
    .by_formant = FALSE,
    .exclude = is.na(.inv_prob),
    .L = weighted.mean(.formant, .inv_prob, na.rm = T),
    .names = "{.formant}_lmw"
  ) |>
  # A weighted Lobanov normalization
  norm_generic(
    F1:F3,
    .by = speaker,
    .by_formant = TRUE,
    .exclude = is.na(.inv_prob),
    .L = weighted.mean(.formant, .inv_prob, na.rm = T),
    .S = sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(.formant, .inv_prob)),
    .names = "{.formant}_zw"
  ) ->
weighted_norm
```
